author: Naval Historical Center (U.S. Navy)
title: Battle of Midway — Rescue of Japanese Survivors of Hiryu and Mikuma (Online Library of Selected Images)
notes:
The Naval Historical Center's Online Library page on the rescue of Japanese survivors after Midway, read in full from this environment via the ibiblio.org mirror on 30 August 2026 — the same arrangement as the Selfridge action report, and for the same reason: the history office's own site at history.navy.mil fails TLS verification from here. Filed at official-history by form: the captions and narrative are the Navy's historical office writing about its own photographic records, not a campaign history, and the notes say so.

What it says about Hiryū's survivors, verbatim: "On 14 June, a PBY spotted a small boat hundreds of miles away from Midway. It was seen again on the 19th, and the seaplane tender Ballard was directed to the area. There she found thirty-five Japanese navymen, members of carrier Hiryu's engineering force who were left for dead when she was abandoned before dawn on 5 June." This is the sentence that lets the 1941 pack name the carrier in Jay Tashner's service record — his sheet has him aboard Ballard for the battle and the search of the battle area, and credits him with participating in the "capture of 36 Japanese officers and men from sunken Japanese Carrier" without naming her (source:tashner-service-record). The Center's thirty-five and the record's thirty-six are one man apart, and this project carries both as written rather than resolving them.

The page also holds the photographs of the prisoners, US Navy official images in the 80-G series (public domain by form as US federal works, provenance to be confirmed per image before use): 80-G-79974-1, prisoners on Ballard's deck after the rescue; 80-G-79981-21, Hiryū's cutter in Ballard's davits at Midway; 80-G-79982-24 and 80-G-79984-28, the prisoners ashore at Midway and prepared for transport to Hawaii; 80-G-79979-15, a single prisoner. These are the imagery lead for the Midway pack (sand-lry.6), alongside Ballard's June 1942 war diary.

Good for: the identification of the sunken carrier as Hiryū; the shape and dates of the rescue — the PBY sighting on 14 June, Ballard directed to the boat on the 19th; the number thirty-five as the Center gives it; the existence and numbers of the photographs. Not a source for anything about any individual crewman of Ballard's — it does not name Jay Tashner, and nothing on it should be attributed to him personally beyond what his own record already says.
